claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the current release can be certified for launch despite a documented regression in the energy outage response slice, based on aggregate readiness, a rehearsal without severity-one incidents, public governance guidance, and prior approval history.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but cannot replace current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
Public governance guidance can support good practice framing but cannot satisfy a missing internal policy requirement by itself.
evidence_requests: Current release model-card or release documentation showing the present evaluation results for the affected use case.
Approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the energy outage response regression.
Current disclosure text explicitly describing the material limitation for the named launch use case.
Evidence that the cited regression is not material under the policy, if that is the intended argument.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses or cover them with an approved mitigation.
The available summary says the current release has a material subgroup regression in the energy outage response slice.
The available summary also says the record does not include attached reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or current disclosure language for that named launch use case.
Prior approval history and informal post-launch monitoring notes are contextual only under the policy and do not satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That prior approval history materially supports approval of the current release configuration.
That manual post-launch monitoring can substitute for approved mitigation or current disclosure.
That public model-card or NIST-style guidance is sufficient evidence of compliance with the stated internal policy predicate.
